name: Floyd-Warshall Algorithm
description: All-pairs shortest path algorithm using dynamic programming. Iteratively considers each vertex as an intermediate node, finding shortest paths between all pairs.
aim: Find shortest paths between ALL pairs of vertices using O(V³) DP: dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k]+dist[k][j]) for each intermediate vertex k.
howItWorks: Initialize distance matrix with direct edge weights, 0 on diagonal, ∞ for no edge
For each intermediate vertex k (0 to V-1):
For each pair (i,j): update dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j])
After V iterations, dist[i][j] holds shortest path from i to j

realWorld: All-pairs shortest paths in small networks
alternatives: Dijkstra from all vertices — O(V(V+E)log V), better for sparse graphs
Bellman-Ford from all vertices — O(V²E), handles negative edges
